text:
Sam: Quick heads-up — saw p95 jump on host-side trace after r21145. Profiling shows a big chunk of time in request parse + stream coalesce. Attaching snippet.

Lia: ugh. which path? ingress or host-proxy?

Kevin: host-ingress, http/2 backpressure pattern + lots of small chunks. KV cache hit-ratio dipped ~2% at the same time.

Sam: logs:
```
parse_ms.p50=0.9 parse_ms.p95=3.9 -> 15.2
coalesce_ms.p95=0.2 -> 5.1
http2_window_wait_ms.avg=0.4 http2_window_wait_ms.p95=4.6
kvcache_hit=0.88 -> 0.86
```

Alex: that coalesce jump smells like an extra copy in the header/body path when frames are <512B. r21145 added extra header normalization for conformance.

Cheng: could also be an interaction with kernel selection / batching heuristics — tiny requests bypass batching, we fall back to a lower-throughput kernel that has worse latency for short seqs.

Lia: can you run a focused microbench (10k qps) with varying frame sizes? I want the frame-size -> p95 curve.

Sam: quick run saved as gist. Command I used: `python tools/bench/ingress_bench.py --qps=10k --frame=256 --duration=60` Result snapshot: p50=42ms p95=260ms (baseline ~98ms p95).

Kevin: proposed short-term mitigations: 1) add a header fast-path for common cases (no-normalize), 2) lower coalesce threshold from 512 -> 128 for small requests, 3) change batching heuristic to use sequence-length histogram when deciding kernel hint.

Alex: also consider a tiny per-request KV prefetch for the common prefix tokens so kvcache hit-ratio doesn't droop on churn bursts. cheap and could buy tail reduction.

perf-bot: perf regression detected: r21145 (author: @alex) CI snapshots show p95 delta +1.7x on small-seq workloads and coalesce_ms p95 increased 4.6x.

Sam: I hacked a sandbox: lowered coalesce to 128 and added header fast-path. Re-ran the bench:
```
before: p95=260ms
after:  p95=120ms
kvcache_hit=0.89
```

Cheng: nice improvement. still seeing intermittent tails at ~180ms (1 in 10k). Might be http2 flow-control blocking or the grpc framing path hitting writev backpressure.

Lia: for safety we should A/B rollout this on the ingress-small-req route: 10% rollout with automatic fallback to previous behavior if p95 regresses. Add observability: ingress_parse_ms, http2_wait_ms, coalesce_writes, kv_hit_rate.

Kevin: I'll add the metrics and a small synthetic that exercises the small-chunk path. Also adding a kernel-hint flag computed from a 1-minute seq-length histogram so we select low-latency kernel when >70% requests <64 tokens.

Alex: opened a PR with the fast-path + coalesce param: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/+/r21300. Bench results are in the PR description and CI includes a microbench.

Sam: filing a short incident ticket with timeline and mitigation plan, will paste the ticket here. Also pinging @eng-sre for oncall aware rollout.

Cheng: follow-up idea: tune http2 WINDOW update frequency to avoid stalls for many tiny frames; or consider switching small-req route to grpc over http1 for lower framing overhead in the short-term. both have tradeoffs.

Lia: +1 to rollout with 10% then 50% if metrics look good. Keep the kvcache prefetch as a follow-up experiment.

Sam: thanks — next steps: 1) merge PR behind feature flag, 2) enable 10% on ingress-small-req, 3) monitor the new metrics for 6h, 4) escalate to full rollout if stable. Will report back in tomorrow standup.

Alex: update: PR tests green, bench confirms ~2.1x p95 improvement for small frames.

perf-bot: note: slate a revert window in case of regression within 30 mins of rollout.

Sam: cool. I'll update the incident ticket and schedule the rollout. Ping me in DMs for infra creds.

Lia: thanks team. short retro after the rollout please — want to capture the root cause (header normalization + batching heuristic mismatch) and add a unit test in the ingress parser to avoid regressions.
